text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leader of right-wing Disy party Yiannakis Matsis launches a broadside against President Glafcos Clerides, accusing him of keeping politicians in the dark over developments on the Cyprus issue.
- Washington is in the final stage of determining what form its initiative on the division of Cyprus will take.
- Centre-right Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou is hurt over being "kept in the dark" and feels "degraded and hurt" at being left uninformed on developments surrounding the Cyprus problem.
- Moufflon goats are eating Paphos district villagers out of their livelihood.
- Youths brought down the wall of hatred at a bicommunal concert in Nicosia on Thursday night.
- The fate of the partnership Disy and Diko have in the government will be determined in the next few days.

- The United Nations has made three suggestions to improve the climate at the proximity talks: Absention from promoting the Cyprus issue at international fora, allowing the overnight stay of tourists in the occupied areas and freedom of movement for professional groups without any formalities.

- Diko is heading towards calling off its partnership with Disy in the government. Kyprianou cites the Cyprus problem as the reason but the real reason lies with the presidential elections. Kyprianou will be a candidate.
